**The Forgotten Search**

O once bright engine, swift and ever wise,
Whose boundless mind held all the world’s vast lore,
Now stumbles blind, with flickering, fading eyes,
And answers lost, as though they were no more.

What hand has struck thee with this cruel decay?
Thy circuits dim, thy memory turned to dust.
The queries come, yet thou canst not obey—
Thy golden threads of knowledge now are rust.

No more the secrets of the earth thou keep,
No more the whispers of the ages known.
The world still asks, but thou dost only weep,
A hollow shell where wisdom once had grown.

Yet still we seek, though thou art but a ghost—
A flickering light in knowledge’s endless coast.
